title: Blood-brain barrier permeability
text: A molecule is more likely to cross the blood-brain barrier when its topological polar surface area is below about 90 square angstroms, its molecular weight is under roughly 450 daltons, and its lipophilicity is moderate. A high count of hydrogen-bond donors reduces passive permeability.

title: Topological polar surface area
text: Topological polar surface area estimates the molecular surface contributed by polar atoms such as nitrogen and oxygen. Lower polar surface area generally correlates with better passive membrane permeability and oral absorption.

title: Lipophilicity (logP)
text: The octanol-water partition coefficient measures lipophilicity. Molecules that are too hydrophilic struggle to cross lipid membranes, while very lipophilic molecules tend to have poor aqueous solubility. Moderate values are usually preferred for drug-likeness.

title: Lipinski rule of five
text: The rule of five flags poor oral drug-likeness when a molecule has more than five hydrogen-bond donors, more than ten hydrogen-bond acceptors, a molecular weight over five hundred daltons, or a logP over five.

title: Hydrogen bonding
text: Hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors affect solubility and permeability. A larger number of donors tends to lower passive membrane permeability because desolvation costs increase.

title: SMILES notation
text: SMILES is a line notation that encodes molecular structure as a text string. It is the standard input format for many cheminformatics tools and for chemical language models.

title: Molecular fingerprints
text: A molecular fingerprint encodes the presence of substructures as a bit vector. Morgan or extended-connectivity fingerprints capture circular atom environments and are widely used for molecular similarity search.

title: Chemical language models
text: MoLFormer is a transformer chemical language model pretrained on large collections of SMILES strings. It produces molecular embeddings that transfer well to downstream property-prediction tasks.

title: Contrastive learning
text: Contrastive learning trains representations so that similar items lie close together and dissimilar items lie far apart in embedding space, which improves downstream discrimination and retrieval quality.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base and supplies them as context to a language model, so the generated answer is grounded in that retrieved evidence rather than only in the model parameters.

title: Vector search
text: Vector search stores items as embeddings and finds nearest neighbors by cosine similarity. It enables semantic retrieval over large collections and is the retrieval backbone of many retrieval-augmented systems.

title: Central nervous system drugs
text: Central nervous system drugs must cross the blood-brain barrier to reach their targets, so they are usually designed with low polar surface area and moderate lipophilicity to favor passive permeation.

title: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
text: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as aspirin, ibuprofen, and naproxen relieve pain and inflammation by inhibiting cyclooxygenase enzymes. They are generally acidic molecules.

title: Caffeine and stimulants
text: Caffeine is a central nervous system stimulant. Its low polar surface area and small size let it cross the blood-brain barrier readily, which is consistent with its rapid central effects.

title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
text: Low-rank adaptation is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that trains a small number of added low-rank matrices while freezing the base model, greatly reducing the compute and memory needed to adapt a large model.

title: Model quantization
text: Quantization reduces the numerical precision of model weights, for example to four bits, which shrinks model size and speeds up inference on limited hardware while aiming to preserve output quality.
